_comment: The attack surface each project is ALLOWED to have. scripts/surface.mjs
compares this against what the manifests and the source actually do, and
fails when a project exceeds its budget.
This file is the security card in every project's README, in machine-
readable form. The README says '01 asks for no permissions'; this is what
stops that sentence from quietly becoming false. Growing a budget is a
deliberate edit to a reviewed file, which is the point: the diff that adds
a permission is the diff a reviewer needs to see.
Every complete project must appear here. An unlisted project fails rather
than being skipped — otherwise adding 04-something would escape the
budget entirely by having no budget.

why: Two hosts, repository-wide: Temporal Cloud, and a local `temporal server start-dev`.
A content script matching anything else — and above all <all_urls> or *://*/* —
means the extension runs on pages that have nothing to do with Temporal.
Self-hosted UIs live on hosts we cannot enumerate, so a fork adds its own host
here on purpose; that is a decision, not a default.
Every one of these turns workflow data into executable markup or code.
The extension renders strings it did not author — workflow ids, types, task
queue names — into a page it does not own. `textContent` cannot execute;
`innerHTML` can, and a workflow id is a perfectly good place to hide a
payload. There is no allowance list here on purpose: if a project ever needs
one of these, that is an edit to this file plus a written reason, reviewed.
Deliberately NOT budgeted here, and this note is what stops that reading as an
oversight. The policy is still the same: browser APIs and code in this
repository for anything specific to this extension — the page-world technique,
the request ledger, what may be sent to a codec server, what is rendered as
text — and mature, maintained libraries for generic algorithms.
What was removed is the machinery: per-project direct/also_bundled lists,
checked against esbuild's metafile, plus a rule that every bundled package be
documented in the README at the installed version and licence. It worked, and
it cost more to read than it caught. Each project's README now carries a short
hand-written table instead, `npm run measure` prints what is really in the
bundles, and the thing that stops a package arriving unreviewed is the
package-lock.json diff.
What that gives up, stated plainly: nothing mechanical now announces a new
TRANSITIVE package. A dependency diff grants the extension no new capability —
it is not a manifest permission diff — but it is an audit-surface diff, and a
reviewer has to read the lockfile to see it.
No gate can read a binary. Not this one, not the leak gate, not any secret
scanner — so a committed image is a file nobody reviews. The icons are
exempt because they are GENERATED from arithmetic by scripts/make-icons.mjs;
the reviewable artefact is that script.
Adding a screenshot or a GIF means adding it here, and it must have been
captured against `temporal server start-dev` with synthetic workflow names.
A recording of a real tenant cannot be redacted after the fact.

01-family-tree.why: The whole claim of this project is that a useful view costs nothing. No permissions key, no service worker, and no chrome.* call in src/ — enforced here and by tsconfig.json's "types": [].

02-techniques.why: One permission, `storage`, for the user's own deep-link templates and toggles. Still no host_permissions — but read the next sentences, because this project DOES originate requests and no manifest key says so. Two per running row: one history-reverse page of one event for the `Last event` column, and one DescribeWorkflowExecution for the retrying-activity badge (pendingActivities is in no other response, which is the justification for the whole request path). Both are issued from the page's own world, by src/page/pageApi.ts and nothing else, where a host permission would buy nothing: Chrome treats a content-script fetch as cross-origin even with one. There is ONE gate, not one per feature — fetchForListedRun() is the only route to the page's Authorization header and it checks the ledger itself, so a feature added later cannot forget to. There is no other outbound host in this project and no setting that can add one: it decodes no payload, and the retry badge deliberately does not read lastFailure.message, so nothing here reads application data. The deep-link card on a single workflow's page fetches nothing at all — it reads responses the page fetched for itself, through the watcher seam in pageApi.ts, which touches neither the ledger nor the credentials. The codec server, the first external egress and the personal-data question all arrive together in stage 03, the payload stage. A permission diff is not a capability diff; the audit for this project is that security card, not this list alone.

03-payloads.why: THE SAME MANIFEST BUDGET AS 02, AND THAT IS THE WARNING THIS ENTRY EXISTS TO CARRY. One permission, `storage`, no host_permissions, no service worker, the same three content-script matches — every capability-bearing key is identical, and a manifest diff against 02 shows the name, the description, the version and the button's tooltip. It bundles the same two packages as 02, too: this stage adds none of its own, having tried three ways to format JSON and kept none of them. What changed is the capability: this is the first project that can send data OUT of the browser, the first that decodes payloads at all, and therefore the first whose panel can hold personal or financial data. No manifest key says any of that, and no permission budget can, which is why this entry is the floor and not the audit. The audit is the security card in 03-payloads/README.md, where the egress is described request-for-request, the two credential options are shown as deliberate deletions, and the residual forged-message risk is stated once at full width along with the argument for accepting it. The egress claims are asserted from outside the extension in 03-payloads/tests/unit/apiInjectCodec.spec.ts, and the endpoint policy they rest on in 03-payloads/tests/unit/codec.spec.ts.
